questions.question: Distinguish between generalized and specialized transduction.
questions.solution_html:
• The process of genetic recombination occurs when a bacteriophage (phage virus) transfers
  • DNA from one bacterium to another.
  • Generalized Transduction
  • ▪ Occurs during the lytic cycle of a phage.
  • ▪ Any random gene from the donor bacterium may be transferred.
  • ▪ Happens when the phage mistakenly packages bacterial DNA into its
  • capsid.
  • ▪ Occurs frequently in the phage life cycle.
  • Specialized Transduction
  • ▪ Occurs during the lysogenic cycle of a temperate phage.
  • ▪ Only specific genes near the phage integration site are transferred.
  • ▪ Happens when the phage incorrectly excises from the bacterial
  • chromosome, taking adjacent genes with it.
  • ▪ Occurs rarely compared to generalized transduction.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
questions.final_answer: ▪ Occurs rarely compared to generalized transduction.

questions.question: Write short notes on terrestrial and aquatic forms of algae.
questions.solution_html:
• Aquatic Algae: Found in water bodies such as ponds, lakes, rivers, and seas. May be free
  • floating (planktonic), swimming (motile), or attached to rocks or submerged surfaces. Include
  • both freshwater and marine forms.(Give any one example for each).
  • Terrestrial Algae: Occur on land, particularly in moist or damp habitats such as soil, tree
  • trunks, rocks, and walls. Based on habitat, terrestrial algae are divided into: a. Saprophytic
  • Forms: Grow on damp soil, rocks, or tree surfaces.eg; Vaucheria b. Cryptophytic Forms: Grow
  • Page3
  • inside the soil and contribute to nitrogen fixation and soil fertility . Examples: Nostoc
  • Anabaena, Trentipohlia etc) Symbiotic Forms: Some algae form symbiotic associations with
  • fungi to produce lichens, which can grow on rocks, tree bark, and walls.
